name: Exfiltration over USB
description: Adversaries may attempt to exfiltrate data over a USB connected physical device. In certain circumstances, such as an air-gapped network compromise, exfiltration could occur via a USB device introduced by a user. The USB device could be used as the final exfiltration point or to hop between otherwise disconnected systems.

telemetry.name: Drive Creation
telemetry.description: Appearance or creation of a drive/device mapping on a host.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect OS device/mount events plus read-only volume inventory; distinguish physical attachment, partition creation and logical mapping.

providers.name: osquery
providers.scope: Scheduled host-state queries; supported tables and privileges vary by OS. Select a table that actually exposes the required object.

providers.name: Linux Audit plus inventory snapshots
providers.scope: Events explain changes; snapshots describe state at collection time.

configuration: Define the inventory query, allowed host set, interval and least-privileged reader. Store a stable asset ID, observation time and collector version.
Keep successive snapshots and calculate additions, removals and changed attributes. Pair state changes with audit events when available.
Export collector health and missed-poll counts so a missing snapshot is not misclassified as a missing asset.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Snapshots miss short-lived objects and do not identify who caused a change. A generic inventory agent is not guaranteed to expose firmware or kernel-level details.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Compare authorized state snapshots: first-seen drivers/services/modules, unexpected configuration drift and integrity changes. Record collection cadence; absence in a sample is not evidence of deletion.

telemetry.name: File Access
telemetry.description: Access to file objects with user, process and access-right context.
telemetry.collection_focus: Enable Audit File System plus a narrow SACL on a lab directory; on Linux select path/syscall rules and join associated Audit records.

providers.name: Windows Security auditing
providers.scope: Policy-dependent account, object, task and logon records on the host that performs the operation.

configuration: Use a lab-only GPO under Computer Configuration → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Advanced Audit Policy Configuration. Enable the specific subcategory named below.
For object-level auditing, configure a narrow system access control list (SACL) on the test object in addition to policy. Do not audit an entire production directory by default.

Forward Security events from the responsible host or controller; retain subject and target identities, object identifiers, result and original XML. Confirm effective policy with auditpol /get /category:*.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: A policy checkbox alone does not guarantee an event. Host role, SACL, success/failure selection and audit policy precedence matter. Directory changes may arrive as multiple records.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per principal, host and object: unusual access/request rates, new principal-object relationships, and changes outside approved administration windows. Control for service accounts and scheduled directory maintenance.

telemetry.name: File Creation
telemetry.description: Creation or overwrite of a file at an observed path.
telemetry.collection_focus: Scope Sysmon FileCreate (11) to the lab directory; retain the process and file path. Differentiate creation/overwrite if the sensor can.

For Linux or macOS, select the equivalent sensor separately and test its emitted fields; a Windows event ID does not transfer across platforms.

analytics.name: Analytic 0616
analytics.guidance: Detects USB device insertion followed by high-volume or sensitive file access and staging activity by suspicious processes or accounts.

tuning.description: Match data staging or export paths (e.g., *.docx, *.csv, *.db) to USB volume letters.
Limit to users who do not normally use removable devices (e.g., service accounts).
Correlate events within a short period following USB insert (e.g., 5–10 minutes).

analytics.name: Analytic 0617
analytics.guidance: Detects USB block device mount followed by file access in sensitive directories or high-volume copy operations by user-controlled processes.

tuning.description: Look for /media/, /mnt/, /run/media/ paths associated with removable storage.
Detect rsync, cp, tar, zip activity writing to USB mount point.
Define abnormal access patterns (e.g., >100 files in <5 min).

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: Kernel Device Events - USB Block Devices

analytics.name: Analytic 0618
analytics.guidance: Detects external volume mount with Finder, Terminal, or script-initiated file copy from user profiles, sensitive folders, or cloud storage sync directories to USB.

tuning.description: Flag removable volumes with suspicious or default names (e.g., NO NAME, BACKUP_01).
Watch for shell or AppleScript execution tied to USB copy.
Detect repeated or abnormal device mounts during work hours.

log_sources.channel: Volume Mount + Process Trace + File Read

software.name: SPACESHIP
software.description: [SPACESHIP](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0035) copies staged data to removable drives when they are inserted into the system.(Citation: FireEye APT30)

references.description: FireEye Labs. (2015, April). APT30 AND THE MECHANICS OF A LONG-RUNNING CYBER ESPIONAGE OPERATION. Retrieved November 17, 2024.

software.name: Agent.btz
software.description: [Agent.btz](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0092) creates a file named thumb.dd on all USB flash drives connected to the victim. This file contains information about the infected system and activity logs.(Citation: Securelist Agent.btz)

references.description: Gostev, A.. (2014, March 12). Agent.btz: a Source of Inspiration?. Retrieved April 8, 2016.

software.name: Remsec
software.description: [Remsec](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0125) contains a module to move data from airgapped networks to Internet-connected systems by using a removable USB device.(Citation: Kaspersky ProjectSauron Full Report)

references.description: Kaspersky Lab's Global Research & Analysis Team. (2016, August 9). The ProjectSauron APT. Retrieved August 17, 2016.

software.name: USBStealer
software.description: [USBStealer](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0136) exfiltrates collected files via removable media from air-gapped victims.(Citation: ESET Sednit USBStealer 2014)

references.description: Calvet, J. (2014, November 11). Sednit Espionage Group Attacking Air-Gapped Networks. Retrieved January 4, 2017.

software.name: Machete
software.description: [Machete](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0409) has a feature to copy files from every drive onto a removable drive in a hidden folder.(Citation: ESET Machete July 2019)(Citation: Securelist Machete Aug 2014)

references.description: ESET. (2019, July). MACHETE JUST GOT SHARPER Venezuelan government institutions under attack. Retrieved September 13, 2019.
Kaspersky Global Research and Analysis Team. (2014, August 20). El Machete. Retrieved September 13, 2019.

actors.name: Tropic Trooper
actors.description: [Tropic Trooper](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0081) has exfiltrated data using USB storage devices.(Citation: TrendMicro Tropic Trooper May 2020)

references.description: Chen, J.. (2020, May 12). Tropic Trooper’s Back: USBferry Attack Targets Air gapped Environments. Retrieved May 20, 2020.

actors.name: Mustang Panda
actors.description: [Mustang Panda](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0129) has used a customized [PlugX](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0013) variant which could exfiltrate documents from air-gapped networks.(Citation: Avira Mustang Panda January 2020)

references.description: Hamzeloofard, S. (2020, January 31). New wave of PlugX targets Hong Kong | Avira Blog. Retrieved April 13, 2021.

mitigations.name: Limit Hardware Installation
mitigations.description: Limit the use of USB devices and removable media within a network.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.description: Disable Autorun if it is unnecessary. (Citation: Microsoft Disable Autorun) Disallow or restrict removable media at an organizational policy level if they are not required for business operations. (Citation: TechNet Removable Media Control)

references.description: Microsoft. (n.d.). How to disable the Autorun functionality in Windows. Retrieved April 20, 2016.

mitigations.name: Data Loss Prevention
mitigations.description: Data loss prevention can detect and block sensitive data being copied to USB devices.

simulation.prerequisites: Use disposable lab hosts and test accounts, explicit target allowlists, a clean snapshot, bounded egress and a restore plan. Review every candidate and dependency before any execution.

synthetic.purpose: Collection/parser contract exercise, NOT a positive example or detection of this TTP.
